ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $B$. Point $D$ is the foot of the altitude from $B$, with $AD=3$ and $DC=4$. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that in triangle ABC, D is located on side AC, AD is labeled 3, and DC is labeled 4; there is a line segment from B to D, and a right-angle symbol is marked at D, indicating that BD is perpendicular to AC. The problem also gives that triangle ABC is right-angled at B, so AC is the hypotenuse, and D is the foot of the altitude drawn from the right-angle vertex B to the hypotenuse AC. According to the hypotenuse altitude theorem, in a right triangle, the altitude from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse satisfies BD^2 = AD · DC. Given AD = 3 and DC = 4, so BD^2 = 3 × 4 = 12, BD = 2√3. Also AC = AD + DC = 3 + 4 = 7. Taking AC as the base and BD as the height, the area of triangle ABC is (1/2) × AC × BD = (1/2) × 7 × 2√3 = 7√3.

raw_record.question_text: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $B$. Point $D$ is the foot of the altitude from $B$, with $AD=3$ and $DC=4$. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?

method.method_draft: Use the altitude-to-hypotenuse relation. Read that D lies on hypotenuse AC with AD=3 and DC=4, so AC=7. Since BD is the altitude from the right angle B to the hypotenuse, apply BD^2 = AD·DC = 3·4 = 12, hence BD=2√3. Then compute the area using AC as the base and BD as the height: area = (1/2)(7)(2√3)=7√3.
